description: This new data release is a deeply-characterized multi-omic dataset from a heterogeneous participant population. It contains the following experiments: 915 whole-genome sequencing, 915 whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, 492 ATAC-seq, 922 RNA-seq, 1,210 metabolic, 1,211 lipidomic, 690 chemical exposomic, and 612 metallomic. All 956 participants are represented with phenotypic and clinical datasets. The dataset reflects genetic ancestries that are often underrepresented in large-scale genomic studies (including participants with admixed genetic backgrounds) and represents a range of geographic recruitment locations, from community-based health systems to urban medical centers.
studyName: NIH MOHD Consortium: Multi-Omics for Health and Disease

description: This sixth release expands the number of available sequences and analyses by more than 15%. It contains the most complete raw sequencing data available from GA4K, including over 2,200 long-read genome sequences, over 14,000 short-read genome and exome analyses, nearly 400 snapshots of patient transcriptomes and epigenomes in individual cells using single-cell RNA (scRNA) and sc open chromatin (scATAC), over 2,700 whole-genome sequences for methylome interpretation (including bulk bisulfite and PacBio-methyl-tagged HiFi sequencing), and nearly 250 functional assessments in available patient tissues using full length cDNA sequences by IsoSeq (PacBio) methodology. Highlights from this v6 release include more long-read data, newly-described phenotypes associated with rare disease profiles, and sequencing from recently-enrolled individuals.

This fourth release includes an additional 375 cell lines for a total of nearly 900. It also adds three new disease-specific consent groups related to cancer, endometrial cancer, and gastrointestinal cancer. The release provides 50X whole-exome sequencing (WES), 30X whole-genome sequencing (WGS), 100X RNA sequencing, and associated model characteristics (metadata) as available on DepMap.org. It contains the underlying data for 189 new NextGen cancer models profiled in the recently published Neiswender JV, Maffa S, Brenan L, et al. A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models. Nature. 2026;657. [doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7).

This first release from the fourth phase of the eMERGE network includes 23,857 VCF files from GWAS genotyped with Illumina Global Diversity Array, 23,857 polygenic risk scores, both raw (plink2) and adjusted after an ancestry calibration model generated by the Broad Institute, 23,857 genome-informed risk assessment reports, 20,428 MeTree family histories, 19,489 clinical monogenic sequences across 16 genes by Invitae/Labcorp, 11,989 participant surveys collected six months after return of results, and 26,502 electronic health records collected six months after return of results. Approximately half of the participants reflected in the genomic data are individuals not typically involved in research, specifically from groups not well-represented in currently available GWAS datasets.
studyName: eMERGE: electronic MEdical Records and GEnomics
